4. Any existing monitoring, metrics, healthcheck, or logging beyond the defaults. Search the whole repo for anything like prometheus, grafana, loki, otel, exporter, metrics, healthcheck.

Report exact file paths and quote the relevant config blocks (log/stats/api/policy sections, logging config, ports, volumes). Be thorough and specific — I need to know exactly what's there today.

32	        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";

34	
35	        # Keep long-lived / idle WebSocket tunnels alive. nginx's default
36	        # proxy_read_timeout is 60s, which severs any tunnel with no upstream
37	        # data for 60s — e.g. an LLM streaming response that pauses while the
38	        # model "thinks", or an idle SSH-over-proxy session → the client sees
39	        # "other side closed" at ~60s. Raise well above interactive gaps.

1	---
2	- name: Ensure certbot TLS options file is present
3	  ansible.builtin.get_url:
4	    url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/certbot/certbot/master/certbot-nginx/certbot_nginx/_internal/tls_configs/options-ssl-nginx.conf
5	    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/options-ssl-nginx.conf"
6	    mode: "0644"
7	    force: false
8	
9	- name: Ensure DH parameters file is present
10	  ansible.builtin.get_url:
11	    url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/certbot/certbot/master/certbot/certbot/ssl-dhparams.pem
12	    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/ssl-dhparams.pem"
13	    mode: "0644"
14	    force: false
15	
16	- name: Check if real cert exists
17	  ansible.builtin.stat:
18	    path: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/live/{{ domain }}/fullchain.pem"
19	  register: le_real_cert
20	
21	- name: Bootstrap Let's Encrypt certificate
22	  when: not le_real_cert.stat.exists
23	  block:
24	    - name: Start nginx with ACME-only config
25	      community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
26	        project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
27	        services:
28	          - nginx
29	        state: present
30	
31	    - name: Wait for nginx to respond on ACME path
32	      ansible.builtin.uri:
33	        url: "http://{{ domain }}/.well-known/acme-challenge/healthcheck"
34	        status_code: [200, 404]
35	      register: acme_probe
36	      retries: 15
37	      delay: 3
38	      until: acme_probe.status in [200, 404]
39	
40	    - name: Request real certificate from Let's Encrypt
41	      # Kept on ONE line to avoid YAML folded-scalar indentation quirks (more-
42	      # indented lines would be preserved as literal newlines, which breaks the
43	      # quoted --entrypoint argument and docker compose parses it as empty).
44	      ansible.builtin.command:
45	        argv:
46	          - docker
47	          - compose
48	          - run
49	          - --rm
50	          - --entrypoint
51	          - >-
52	            certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/certbot
53	            {% if le_staging | int == 1 %}--staging {% endif %}
54	            --email {{ letsencrypt_email }} -d {{ domain }}
55	            --rsa-key-size {{ le_rsa_key_size }}
56	            --agree-tos --non-interactive --no-eff-email
57	          - certbot
58	        chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
59	      register: certbot_result
60	      changed_when: "'Successfully received certificate' in certbot_result.stdout or 'Certificate not yet due for renewal' in certbot_result.stdout"
61	
62	    - name: Render full nginx config now that cert exists
63	      ansible.builtin.template:
64	        src: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../roles/vpn/templates/nginx/v2ray.conf.j2"
65	        dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/conf.d/v2ray.conf"
66	        owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
67	        group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
68	        mode: "0644"
69	
70	- name: Bring up full compose stack
71	  community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
72	    project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
73	    state: present
74	
75	- name: Reload nginx after bootstrap
76	  ansible.builtin.shell: docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -s reload
77	  args:
78	    chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
79	  when: not le_real_cert.stat.exists
80	  changed_when: true
81

30	        proxy_http_version 1.1;
31	        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
32	        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
33	        proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
34	
35	        # Keep long-lived / idle WebSocket tunnels alive. nginx's default
36	        # proxy_read_timeout is 60s, which severs any tunnel with no upstream
37	        # data for 60s — e.g. an LLM streaming response that pauses while the
38	        # model "thinks", or an idle SSH-over-proxy session → the client sees
39	        # "other side closed" at ~60s. Raise well above interactive gaps.
40	        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
41	        proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
42	    }
43	}

23	    done

36	            for t in "${missing[@]}"; do

45	            fi

48	            if [ $install_uv -eq 1 ]; then

11	brew install just                          # macOS / Linuxbrew
12	# -- or Debian/Ubuntu 24.04+: sudo apt install -y just
13	# -- or prebuilt binary: https://just.systems/
14	
15	just setup                                 # ansible + jq + uv + galaxy collections
16	```
17	
18	`just setup` auto-detects Homebrew (macOS / Linuxbrew) first, falls back to
19	`apt` on Debian/Ubuntu, and prints manual hints everywhere else. It is
20	idempotent, so re-running only installs what is missing.
21	
22	Prefer to do it by hand? Any of these work:
23	
24	```bash
25	# macOS / Linuxbrew:
26	brew install ansible just jq uv
27	
28	# Debian/Ubuntu 24.04+ (older releases ship ancient Ansible; prefer pipx there):
29	sudo apt install -y ansible just jq
30	curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
31	
32	# Anywhere Python is available (works on older distros + Windows/WSL):
33	pipx install ansible-core
34	# then grab `just` from https://just.systems/, `jq` from your package manager,
35	# and `uv` from https://astral.sh/uv/
36	
37	ansible-galaxy install -r ansible/requirements.yml
38	```
39	
40	`just`, `jq`, and `uv` are only needed for the laptop-side helpers
41	(`just deploy`, the Azure throwaway flow, etc.). If you'd rather drive
42	`ansible-playbook` directly, only Ansible itself is required.
43	
44	On the VPS: **nothing Ansible-side.** The playbook connects over SSH as a
45	user with passwordless sudo and installs rootful Docker + everything else
46	itself. All you need on the server is:
47	
48	- `sshd` reachable on port 22 (from your laptop).
49	- A user that can `sudo` without a password prompt.
50	- Ports 22/80/443 open at the cloud firewall (LE's HTTP-01 challenge needs 80
51	  inbound during the first deploy).
52	- Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 is what we test against; other Debian-family distros
53	  should work but aren't in CI.
54	
55	## First-time setup
56	
57	1. **Copy inventory example:**
58	   ```bash
59	   cp ansible/inventory/prod.ini.example ansible/inventory/prod.ini
60	   vim ansible/inventory/prod.ini                # add your host
61	   ```
62	2. **Copy vault example and fill in values:**
63	   ```bash
64	   cp ansible/group_vars/vpn/vault.yml.example ansible/group_vars/vpn/vault.yml
65	   vim ansible/group_vars/vpn/vault.yml          # fill domain, email, uuid
66	   ```
67	3. **Encrypt the vault:**
68	   ```bash
69	   ansible-vault encrypt ansible/group_vars/vpn/vault.yml
70	   ```
71	4. **Store the vault password where Ansible can find it:**
72	   ```bash
73	   echo 'yourpassword' > ~/.vault-pass
74	   chmod 600 ~/.vault-pass
75	   export ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE=~/.vault-pass
76	   ```
77	   Or pass `--ask-vault-pass` each run.
78	
79	## Deploy
80	
81	From the repo root:
82	
83	```bash
84	just deploy                # full: common + docker + vpn + letsencrypt
85	just deploy-fast           # just vpn role (use after config tweaks)
86	just verify                # smoke-test the running deploy
87	just rotate-uuid           # generate a new UUID, update vault, redeploy vpn role
88	```
89	
90	Or directly:
91	
92	```bash
93	cd ansible
94	ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml
95	ansible-playbook playbooks/deploy.yml             # vpn-only, faster
96	ansible-playbook playbooks/rotate-uuid.yml -e new_uuid=$(uuidgen)
97	```
98	
99	## Layout
100	
101	- `ansible.cfg` — inventory path, SSH multiplexing, YAML output.
102	- `requirements.yml` — Ansible collections (`community.docker`, `ansible.posix`, `community.general`).
103	- `inventory/` — `prod.ini.example` and `dev.ini.example`; real `prod.ini`/`dev.ini` are gitignored.
104	- `group_vars/all.yml` — non-secret defaults (tz, deploy path, ports).
105	- `group_vars/vpn/vars.yml` — per-group indirection: `domain: "{{ vault_domain }}"`.
106	- `group_vars/vpn/vault.yml` — single-host encrypted secrets (gitignored). Use this when you maintain one long-lived VPS by hand.
107	- `host_vars/<rg>/vault.yml` — per-host encrypted secrets (gitignored). The Azure throwaway flow (`just az-configure`) writes one per tracked VM. Takes precedence over `group_vars/vpn/vault.yml` when both are present. See [`docs/MULTI-HOST.md`](../docs/MULTI-HOST.md).
108	- `playbooks/site.yml` — full deploy (all roles in order).
109	- `playbooks/deploy.yml` — app-only, for config tweaks.
110	- `playbooks/rotate-uuid.yml` — rotate V2Ray UUID.
111	- `roles/`
112	  - `common/` — OS hardening: apt update, timezone, ufw, fail2ban, unattended-upgrades.
113	  - `docker/` — rootful Docker install + compose plugin + user in docker group.
114	  - `vpn/` — renders server config from Jinja2 templates, syncs compose files, `docker compose up -d`.
115	  - `letsencrypt/` — bootstraps Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 cert on first deploy (subsequent deploys are no-ops since certbot sidecar auto-renews).
116	
117	## Secrets
118	
119	Anything under `group_vars/vpn/vault.yml` is encrypted with `ansible-vault`. Plain values never land in git. If you accidentally commit an unencrypted vault.yml, rotate the UUID immediately and scrub with `git filter-repo`.
120
```

---LOGROTATE DOC---
# Log rotation

Nginx and V2Ray write `access.log` / `error.log` to mounted host directories
under `/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}/`. Without rotation they grow
unbounded and eventually fill the root FS (symptom: `No space left on device`
on `tmux`, `apt`, `docker`, anything).

The Ansible `vpn` role drops `/etc/logrotate.d/vpn` on every deploy.
Ubuntu's pre-installed `/etc/cron.daily/logrotate` picks it up from there —
no cron to schedule, no sidecar to run.

## TL;DR — on a fresh VPS

Already handled by `just deploy` / `just deploy-fast`. Nothing to do.

## TL;DR — patch an already-running VPS without re-deploying

Useful when you've got a live server you don't want to re-Ansible right now
(e.g. disk already 100% full, or VPS predates the repo change). One SSH
session, ~10 seconds:

```bash
ssh <user>@<vps>

# 1. Drop the logrotate config
sudo tee /etc/logrotate.d/vpn > /dev/null <<'EOF'
/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/nginx/*.log
/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/v2ray/*.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    maxsize 20M
    missingok
    notifempty
    compress
    delaycompress
    copytruncate
}
EOF

# 2. Dry-run — confirms logrotate parses it and sees the files
sudo logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.d/vpn

# 3. Force-rotate once to drain the existing backlog
sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/vpn
du -sh /opt/vpn/runtime/logs/*
```

From here `/etc/cron.daily/logrotate` (already wired up on any Ubuntu Server)
takes over — no further action.

The next `just deploy` / `just deploy-fast` will overwrite
`/etc/logrotate.d/vpn` with the template-rendered version, which is
byte-identical to the above — safe to run, no config drift.

## What the config does

| Directive | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| `daily` | Rotate once per day (triggered by `/etc/cron.daily/logrotate`). |
| `rotate 7` | Keep 7 historical files; the 8th is deleted. |
```
</details></tool-use>

# Server-side runtime: current state

## Key finding up front

There is **zero observability tooling today**. No Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Mimir, OpenTelemetry, exporters, `stub_status`, `/metrics` endpoint, V2Ray stats/api, or Docker healthchecks anywhere in the operational code. Logging is entirely file-based: the two long-running apps (nginx, v2ray) write their own `access.log`/`error.log` to bind-mounted host directories, rotated by a host `logrotate` cron. Container stdout/stderr uses Docker's **default `json-file` driver** (never configured explicitly, no `daemon.json`, no `log-opts`, no per-service `logging:` block).

## 1. The Docker Compose stack

Two copies exist and are byte-identical in structure:

- **Source-of-truth / dev reference:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/server/compose.yml`
- **Ansible template (rendered to `/opt/vpn/compose.yml` on the VPS):** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/vpn/templates/compose.yml.j2`

The only differences are Jinja substitutions: `TZ={{ tz }}` (default `Asia/Shanghai`) and `expose: "{{ v2ray_internal_port }}"` (default `30909`). The static compose hardcodes `30909` and `TZ=${TZ:-Asia/Shanghai}`.

**Three services** (no top-level `networks:` block — all share the default compose bridge network; nginx reaches v2ray via a legacy `links:` alias):

### `nginx`
- Image: `nginx:latest`
- `container_name: nginx`, `restart: unless-stopped`
- Ports (host-published): `80:80`, `443:443`
- `links: [v2ray:v2ray]`
- Command runs a 6h reload loop plus `nginx -g "daemon off;"`
- Volumes:
  - `./runtime/nginx/conf.d:/etc/nginx/conf.d:ro`
  - `./static/nginx/html:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro`
  - `./runtime/logs/nginx:/var/log/nginx` (log output — writable bind mount)
  - `./runtime/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt`
  - `./runtime/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot`

### `certbot`
- Image: `certbot/certbot`
- `container_name: certbot`, `restart: unless-stopped`
- No ports
- Entrypoint loops `certbot renew` every 12h
- Volumes: `./runtime/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt`, `./runtime/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot`

### `v2ray`
- Image: `v2ray/official:latest`
- `container_name: v2ray`, `restart: always`
- `environment: TZ=...`
- Command: `v2ray -config=/etc/v2ray/config.json`
- **No published ports** — only `expose: "30909"` (internal-only; reached by nginx over the compose network)
- Volumes:
  - `./runtime/v2ray:/etc/v2ray:ro`
  - `./runtime/logs/v2ray:/var/log/v2ray` (log output — writable bind mount)

**Logging configuration for the stack:** none at the Docker level. No `logging:` driver blocks, no `daemon.json` (confirmed — the `docker` role at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml` just installs Docker via get.docker.com and never writes daemon config). App logs go to host dirs `/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}/` and are rotated by `/etc/logrotate.d/vpn` (see §4).

# V2Ray Ansible Deploy Pipeline — Complete Structure Report

All paths absolute. Root: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray`.

## 1. Playbook wiring

There are **three** playbooks in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/playbooks/`:

**`site.yml`** (full deploy) — targets `hosts: vpn`, `become: true`, `gather_facts: true`. Roles run in this exact order:
```yaml
roles:
  - common
  - docker
  - vpn
  - letsencrypt
```

**`deploy.yml`** (app-only "fast" redeploy) — same host/become/facts, runs **only** `vpn`. Skips OS hardening and Docker install. Note: it does *not* run `letsencrypt`, so `deploy-fast` never brings the compose stack up itself — it relies on the `recreate stack` / `restart v2ray` / `reload nginx` handlers in the vpn role (see §5) firing when a template changes.

**`rotate-uuid.yml`** — targets `hosts: vpn`. Computes `effective_uuid: "{{ new_uuid | default(v2ray_uuid) }}"` in play vars, prints it via a `debug` pre_task, then runs only the `vpn` role with `v2ray_uuid` overridden to `effective_uuid`. It deliberately does **not** edit the vault; the header comment instructs you to `ansible-vault edit` afterward.

**Tags:** none. No `tags:` keys anywhere in the playbooks or roles. Role selection is done by choosing which playbook to run, not by tags.

**Host targeting:** every play targets the group `vpn`. `ansible.cfg` sets `inventory = inventory/prod.ini` as default, `roles_path = roles`, `forks = 10`, host key checking off, SSH pipelining + ControlPersist on.

## 2. Roles under `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/`

There are exactly **four** roles: `common`, `docker`, `vpn`, `letsencrypt`. No others.

### `common` — OS hardening
- `tasks/main.yml`: apt update (cache_valid_time 3600) → install `common_apt_packages` → set timezone (`community.general.timezone` to `{{ tz }}`) → write `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades` (unattended-upgrades) → UFW default deny-in/allow-out → open `firewall_allowed_tcp` ports (loop, proto tcp) → ensure `fail2ban` enabled+started.
- `defaults/main.yml`: `common_apt_packages` = ca-certificates, curl, gnupg, git, vim, tmux, ufw, fail2ban, unattended-upgrades.
- `handlers/main.yml`: one handler `Restart fail2ban` (not currently notified by any task).
- No templates.

### `docker` — rootful Docker install
- `tasks/main.yml`: `docker --version` probe (failed_when false) → **block guarded by `when: docker_version_check.rc != 0`**: get `https://get.docker.com` to `/tmp/get-docker.sh`, run it, remove script → add `docker_users` to `docker` group → enable+start `docker` systemd → apt-install `python3-docker` (needed for the `community.docker` modules used later).
- `defaults/main.yml`: `docker_users: ["{{ ansible_user }}"]`.
- No handlers, no templates.

### `vpn` — renders config + compose into `{{ deploy_path }}` (`/opt/vpn`)
Key file: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/vpn/tasks/main.yml`. Task flow:

1. **Create deploy directory tree** — creates `{{ deploy_path }}` and subdirs `static`, `runtime`, `runtime/nginx/conf.d`, `runtime/v2ray`, `runtime/certbot/conf`, `runtime/certbot/www`, `runtime/logs/nginx`, `runtime/logs/v2ray` (owner/group `ansible_user`, 0755).
2. **Install logrotate config** — templates `logrotate-vpn.conf.j2` → `/etc/logrotate.d/vpn` (root, 0644, `become: true`).
3. **Sync static assets** — `ansible.posix.synchronize` from `vpn_static_src` (`{{ playbook_dir }}/../../server/static`, i.e. `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/server/static`) → `{{ deploy_path }}/static/`, `delete: true`, `delegate_to: localhost`, passes through the inventory private key.
4. **Render compose.yml** — `compose.yml.j2` → `{{ deploy_path }}/compose.yml`. **`notify: recreate stack`**.
5. **Render V2Ray config** — `v2ray/config.json.j2` → `{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/v2ray/config.json` (0640). **`notify: restart v2ray`**.
6. **Stat cert** — checks `{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/live/{{ domain }}/fullchain.pem`, registers `le_cert`.
7. **Conditional nginx config** (the two-phase split lives partly here):
   - `when: le_cert.stat.exists` → render `nginx/v2ray.conf.j2` (full TLS+WS proxy config), **`notify: reload nginx`**.
   - `when: not le_cert.stat.exists` → render `nginx/acme-only.conf.j2` (HTTP-only, serves ACME challenge + 301 redirect). No notify (nginx isn't up yet on first run).

Important: **the vpn role never runs `docker compose up` directly.** It only renders files and fires handlers. Bringing the stack up is the letsencrypt role's job (or handlers on subsequent runs).

`defaults/main.yml`: only `vpn_static_src`.

`handlers/main.yml` — three handlers:
```yaml
- name: Reload nginx        # listen: reload nginx
  community.docker.docker_container_exec: {container: nginx, command: nginx -s reload}
- name: Restart v2ray       # listen: restart v2ray
  community.docker.docker_container: {name: v2ray, state: started, restart: true}
- name: Recreate compose stack   # listen: recreate stack
  community.docker.docker_compose_v2: {project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}", state: present}
```

Templates under `roles/vpn/templates/`:
- `compose.yml.j2` — three services: `nginx` (ports 80/443, mounts runtime confs, static html, certbot conf+www, logs; `links: v2ray:v2ray`), `certbot` (renew loop every 12h), `v2ray` (image `v2ray/official:latest`, `expose: {{ v2ray_internal_port }}`, config mounted read-only). No monitoring/metrics services currently.
- `v2ray/config.json.j2` — vmess inbound on `v2ray_internal_port`, ws path `v2ray_ws_path`, client id `v2ray_uuid`, alterId 64; freedom outbound; logs to `/var/log/v2ray/{access,error}.log`.

- `nginx/acme-only.conf.j2` — HTTP-only bootstrap config.

### `letsencrypt` — two-phase cert bootstrap
Key file: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`. Flow:

1. **Fetch TLS helper files** (idempotent, `force: false`): `options-ssl-nginx.conf` and `ssl-dhparams.pem` into `{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/`.
2. **Stat real cert** → registers `le_real_cert` (same fullchain path as the vpn role checks).
3. **Bootstrap block, `when: not le_real_cert.stat.exists`** (this is phase 1 → phase 2):
   - **Start nginx only** with `docker_compose_v2` (`services: [nginx]`, `state: present`) — nginx comes up serving the ACME-only config that the vpn role rendered.
   - **Wait for ACME path** — `uri` GET `http://{{ domain }}/.well-known/acme-challenge/healthcheck`, accepts 200/404, retries 15 × delay 3s.
   - **Request real cert** — raw `ansible.builtin.command` running `docker compose run --rm --entrypoint "certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/certbot [--staging] --email … -d {{ domain }} --rsa-key-size {{ le_rsa_key_size }} --agree-tos --non-interactive --no-eff-email" certbot` with `chdir: {{ deploy_path }}`. `--staging` is injected when `le_staging | int == 1`.

4. **Bring up full compose stack** — `docker_compose_v2` `project_src: {{ deploy_path }}`, `state: present` (runs every deploy, idempotent).
5. **Reload nginx after bootstrap** — `docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -s reload` (chdir deploy_path), `when: not le_real_cert.stat.exists` only.

`defaults/main.yml`: `le_rsa_key_size: 4096`, `le_staging: 0`. No handlers, no templates of its own (reuses the vpn role's).

## 4. Justfile

File: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/Justfile`. Vars: `ansible_dir := "ansible"`, `ansible_opts := env_var_or_default("ANSIBLE_OPTS", "")`. Every recipe:

- **`vault-encrypt rg=""`** — mirror of the above for `ansible-vault encrypt`.
- **`az-up *args`** → `scripts/az_up.sh` (provision Azure VM + DNS).
- **`az-configure *args`** → `scripts/az_configure.py` (renders inventory + per-host vaults).
- **`az-client *args`** → `scripts/vmess_client.py` (generate client configs).
- **`az-down *args`** → `scripts/az_down.sh` (tear down one RG).
- **`az-rotate-ip *args`** → `scripts/az_rotate_ip.sh`.

- **`az-cycle`** — full single-VM loop: az_up → az_configure → `just deploy` → `just verify` → vmess_client → pause → `az_down`. Sets `ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to `.secrets/.vault-pass`.

- **`test-up` (deps: test-setup)** — `cd test && docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d --build`.

**Bringing services up/down:** there is no laptop-side "down" recipe for prod. Up = `just deploy` / `deploy-fast` (via the roles). `just ps` inspects status. `just test-up`/`test-down` manage the local Docker test container only.

**`scripts/verify.sh`** (135 lines) — resolves `DOMAIN` (explicit env, or from `.secrets/azure/vms/<rg>.json`), then smoke-tests: `curl` HTTPS `/` (expects a code), `curl` HTTPS `/v2ray`, and TLS chain validity via `openssl s_client … grep 'Verify return code: 0'`. On failure it prints the nginx/v2ray log tail commands.

## 5. How compose is invoked

`community.docker.docker_compose_v2` and raw `docker compose` are called in **four** places, all pointing at `project_src` / `chdir` = `{{ deploy_path }}` (= `/opt/vpn`), which uses the rendered `/opt/vpn/compose.yml`:

1. **`ansible/roles/vpn/handlers/main.yml`** — handler `Recreate compose stack`:
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     state: present
   ```
   Fired via `notify: recreate stack` when `compose.yml` changes. (Same file also has `docker_container_exec` for nginx reload and `docker_container` restart for v2ray — container-scoped, not compose.)

2. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — "Start nginx with ACME-only config" (phase 1):
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     services: [nginx]
     state: present
   ```

3. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — cert request uses raw CLI:
   ```yaml
   ansible.builtin.command:
     argv: [docker, compose, run, --rm, --entrypoint, "certbot certonly …", certbot]
     chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
   ```

4. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — "Bring up full compose stack" (phase 2, every run):
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     state: present
   ```
   Plus the post-bootstrap `docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -s reload` (chdir `{{ deploy_path }}`).

The `just ps` recipe also calls `docker compose -f /opt/vpn/compose.yml ps` remotely.

## Mental model / where a monitoring role slots in

- The pipeline is: **`common` (harden) → `docker` (install) → `vpn` (render `/opt/vpn/{compose.yml, runtime/*, static/*}`, notify handlers) → `letsencrypt` (cert bootstrap + `docker compose up` the whole stack)**. The stack is a single compose project at `/opt/vpn/compose.yml` with `nginx`, `certbot`, `v2ray`.
- A **per-server metrics/log agent** fits cleanly as (a) a new service block appended to `compose.yml.j2` mounting `runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}` + host metrics, or (b) a new role `monitoring-agent` added to `site.yml` after `vpn`. Because the vpn role owns `compose.yml`, adding the agent as a compose service and letting the `recreate stack` handler bring it up is the most convention-consistent path. Firewall: agent egress is allowed by default (UFW allow-out); if the agent needs an inbound scrape port, add it to `firewall_allowed_tcp` in `group_vars/all.yml`.
- A **central observability stack** needs a new inventory group (e.g. `[observability]`) and a new play (in `site.yml` or a dedicated `playbooks/observability.yml`) targeting it, plus its own role rendering its own compose project under a separate `deploy_path` — mirroring the existing `deploy_path`/render/`docker_compose_v2` pattern. Config knobs go in `group_vars/all.yml` (or a new group_vars file); secrets go through the `vault_*` → plain-name indirection in `group_vars/vpn/vars.yml`.
- Note the `deploy-fast` gotcha: since `deploy.yml` runs only the vpn role, a monitoring service added to `compose.yml.j2` will come up on fast deploys via the `recreate stack` handler (which changes to the template will trigger), so no extra `docker compose up` task is strictly required in the vpn role.

No monitoring, metrics, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki, or log-shipping code exists in the repo today — this is a greenfield addition.

## 1. Playbook wiring

There are **three** playbooks in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/playbooks/`:

**`site.yml`** (full deploy) — targets `hosts: vpn`, `become: true`, `gather_facts: true`. Roles run in this exact order:
```yaml
roles:
  - common
  - docker
  - vpn
  - letsencrypt
```

**`deploy.yml`** (app-only "fast" redeploy) — same host/become/facts, runs **only** `vpn`. Skips OS hardening and Docker install. Note: it does *not* run `letsencrypt`, so `deploy-fast` never brings the compose stack up itself — it relies on the `recreate stack` / `restart v2ray` / `reload nginx` handlers in the vpn role (see §5) firing when a template changes.

**`rotate-uuid.yml`** — targets `hosts: vpn`. Computes `effective_uuid: "{{ new_uuid | default(v2ray_uuid) }}"` in play vars, prints it via a `debug` pre_task, then runs only the `vpn` role with `v2ray_uuid` overridden to `effective_uuid`. It deliberately does **not** edit the vault; the header comment instructs you to `ansible-vault edit` afterward.

**Tags:** none. No `tags:` keys anywhere in the playbooks or roles. Role selection is done by choosing which playbook to run, not by tags.

**Host targeting:** every play targets the group `vpn`. `ansible.cfg` sets `inventory = inventory/prod.ini` as default, `roles_path = roles`, `forks = 10`, host key checking off, SSH pipelining + ControlPersist on.

## 2. Roles under `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/`

There are exactly **four** roles: `common`, `docker`, `vpn`, `letsencrypt`. No others.

### `common` — OS hardening
- `tasks/main.yml`: apt update (cache_valid_time 3600) → install `common_apt_packages` → set timezone (`community.general.timezone` to `{{ tz }}`) → write `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades` (unattended-upgrades) → UFW default deny-in/allow-out → open `firewall_allowed_tcp` ports (loop, proto tcp) → ensure `fail2ban` enabled+started.
- `defaults/main.yml`: `common_apt_packages` = ca-certificates, curl, gnupg, git, vim, tmux, ufw, fail2ban, unattended-upgrades.
- `handlers/main.yml`: one handler `Restart fail2ban` (not currently notified by any task).
- No templates.

### `docker` — rootful Docker install
- `tasks/main.yml`: `docker --version` probe (failed_when false) → **block guarded by `when: docker_version_check.rc != 0`**: get `https://get.docker.com` to `/tmp/get-docker.sh`, run it, remove script → add `docker_users` to `docker` group → enable+start `docker` systemd → apt-install `python3-docker` (needed for the `community.docker` modules used later).
- `defaults/main.yml`: `docker_users: ["{{ ansible_user }}"]`.
- No handlers, no templates.

### `vpn` — renders config + compose into `{{ deploy_path }}` (`/opt/vpn`)
Key file: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/ansible/roles/vpn/tasks/main.yml`. Task flow:

1. **Create deploy directory tree** — creates `{{ deploy_path }}` and subdirs `static`, `runtime`, `runtime/nginx/conf.d`, `runtime/v2ray`, `runtime/certbot/conf`, `runtime/certbot/www`, `runtime/logs/nginx`, `runtime/logs/v2ray` (owner/group `ansible_user`, 0755).
2. **Install logrotate config** — templates `logrotate-vpn.conf.j2` → `/etc/logrotate.d/vpn` (root, 0644, `become: true`).
3. **Sync static assets** — `ansible.posix.synchronize` from `vpn_static_src` (`{{ playbook_dir }}/../../server/static`, i.e. `/Users/david/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray/server/static`) → `{{ deploy_path }}/static/`, `delete: true`, `delegate_to: localhost`, passes through the inventory private key.
4. **Render compose.yml** — `compose.yml.j2` → `{{ deploy_path }}/compose.yml`. **`notify: recreate stack`**.
5. **Render V2Ray config** — `v2ray/config.json.j2` → `{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/v2ray/config.json` (0640). **`notify: restart v2ray`**.
6. **Stat cert** — checks `{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/live/{{ domain }}/fullchain.pem`, registers `le_cert`.
7. **Conditional nginx config** (the two-phase split lives partly here):
   - `when: le_cert.stat.exists` → render `nginx/v2ray.conf.j2` (full TLS+WS proxy config), **`notify: reload nginx`**.
   - `when: not le_cert.stat.exists` → render `nginx/acme-only.conf.j2` (HTTP-only, serves ACME challenge + 301 redirect). No notify (nginx isn't up yet on first run).

Important: **the vpn role never runs `docker compose up` directly.** It only renders files and fires handlers. Bringing the stack up is the letsencrypt role's job (or handlers on subsequent runs).

`defaults/main.yml`: only `vpn_static_src`.

`handlers/main.yml` — three handlers:
```yaml
- name: Reload nginx        # listen: reload nginx
  community.docker.docker_container_exec: {container: nginx, command: nginx -s reload}
- name: Restart v2ray       # listen: restart v2ray
  community.docker.docker_container: {name: v2ray, state: started, restart: true}
- name: Recreate compose stack   # listen: recreate stack

```

Templates under `roles/vpn/templates/`:
- `compose.yml.j2` — three services: `nginx` (ports 80/443, mounts runtime confs, static html, certbot conf+www, logs; `links: v2ray:v2ray`), `certbot` (renew loop every 12h), `v2ray` (image `v2ray/official:latest`, `expose: {{ v2ray_internal_port }}`, config mounted read-only). - **`deploy`** — `cd ansible &amp;&amp; ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml {{ansible_opts}}` (full: common+docker+vpn+letsencrypt).
- **`deploy-fast`** — `ansible-playbook playbooks/deploy.yml {{ansible_opts}}` (vpn role only).
- **`rotate-uuid`** — `ansible-playbook playbooks/rotate-uuid.yml -e new_uuid=$(uuidgen) {{ansible_opts}}`.
- **`verify *args`** — runs `scripts/verify.sh {{args}}` (see §details below).
- **`logs-v2ray`** — `ansible vpn -a "tail -n 50 /opt/vpn/runtime/logs/v2ray/access.log"`.
- **`logs-nginx`** — `ansible vpn -a "tail -n 50 /opt/vpn/runtime/logs/nginx/error.log"`.
- **`ps`** — `ansible vpn -a "docker compose -f /opt/vpn/compose.yml ps"` (compose service status on the VPS).
- **`vault-edit rg=""`** — `ansible-vault edit` on `host_vars/&lt;rg&gt;/vault.yml` or legacy `group_vars/vpn/vault.yml`; detects multi-host layout and demands `&lt;rg&gt;`.
- **`vault-encrypt rg=""`** — mirror of the above for `ansible-vault encrypt`.
- **`az-up *args`** → `scripts/az_up.sh` (provision Azure VM + DNS).
- **`az-configure *args`** → `scripts/az_configure.py` (renders inventory + per-host vaults).
- **`az-client *args`** → `scripts/vmess_client.py` (generate client configs).
- **`az-down *args`** → `scripts/az_down.sh` (tear down one RG).
- **`az-rotate-ip *args`** → `scripts/az_rotate_ip.sh`.
- **`az-list`** — jq-formats `.secrets/azure/vms/*.json`.
- **`az-cycle`** — full single-VM loop: az_up → az_configure → `just deploy` → `just verify` → vmess_client → pause → `az_down`. Sets `ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to `.secrets/.vault-pass`.
- **`test-setup`** — generate throwaway SSH keypair at `test/ssh/id_ed25519`.
- **`test-up` (deps: test-setup)** — `cd test &amp;&amp; docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d --build`.
- **`test-ping`** — `ansible -i inventory/test.ini vpn -m ping`.
- **`test-down`** — `cd test &amp;&amp; docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down -v`.

**Bringing services up/down:** there is no laptop-side "down" recipe for prod. Up = `just deploy` / `deploy-fast` (via the roles). `just ps` inspects status. `just test-up`/`test-down` manage the local Docker test container only.

**`scripts/verify.sh`** (135 lines) — resolves `DOMAIN` (explicit env, or from `.secrets/azure/vms/&lt;rg&gt;.json`), then smoke-tests: `curl` HTTPS `/` (expects a code), `curl` HTTPS `/v2ray`, and TLS chain validity via `openssl s_client … grep 'Verify return code: 0'`. On failure it prints the nginx/v2ray log tail commands.

## 5. How compose is invoked

`community.docker.docker_compose_v2` and raw `docker compose` are called in **four** places, all pointing at `project_src` / `chdir` = `{{ deploy_path }}` (= `/opt/vpn`), which uses the rendered `/opt/vpn/compose.yml`:

1. **`ansible/roles/vpn/handlers/main.yml`** — handler `Recreate compose stack`:
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     state: present
   ```
   Fired via `notify: recreate stack` when `compose.yml` changes. (Same file also has `docker_container_exec` for nginx reload and `docker_container` restart for v2ray — container-scoped, not compose.)

2. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — "Start nginx with ACME-only config" (phase 1):
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     services: [nginx]
     state: present
   ```

3. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — cert request uses raw CLI:
   ```yaml
   ansible.builtin.command:
     argv: [docker, compose, run, --rm, --entrypoint, "certbot certonly …", certbot]
     chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
   ```

4. **`ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`** — "Bring up full compose stack" (phase 2, every run):
   ```yaml
   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
     project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
     state: present
   ```
   Plus the post-bootstrap `docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -s reload` (chdir `{{ deploy_path }}`).

The `just ps` recipe also calls `docker compose -f /opt/vpn/compose.yml ps` remotely.

---

## Mental model / where a monitoring role slots in

- The pipeline is: **`common` (harden) → `docker` (install) → `vpn` (render `/opt/vpn/{compose.yml, runtime/*, static/*}`, notify handlers) → `letsencrypt` (cert bootstrap + `docker compose up` the whole stack)**. The stack is a single compose project at `/opt/vpn/compose.yml` with `nginx`, `certbot`, `v2ray`.
- A **per-server metrics/log agent** fits cleanly as (a) a new service block appended to `compose.yml.j2` mounting `runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}` + host metrics, or (b) a new role `monitoring-agent` added to `site.yml` after `vpn`. Because the vpn role owns `compose.yml`, adding the agent as a compose service and letting the `recreate stack` handler bring it up is the most convention-consistent path. Firewall: agent egress is allowed by default (UFW allow-out); if the agent needs an inbound scrape port, add it to `firewall_allowed_tcp` in `group_vars/all.yml`.
- A **central observability stack** needs a new inventory group (e.g. `[observability]`) and a new play (in `site.yml` or a dedicated `playbooks/observability.yml`) targeting it, plus its own role rendering its own compose project under a separate `deploy_path` — mirroring the existing `deploy_path`/render/`docker_compose_v2` pattern. Config knobs go in `group_vars/all.yml` (or a new group_vars file); secrets go through the `vault_*` → plain-name indirection in `group_vars/vpn/vars.yml`.
- Note the `deploy-fast` gotcha: since `deploy.yml` runs only the vpn role, a monitoring service added to `compose.yml.j2` will come up on fast deploys via the `recreate stack` handler (which changes to the template will trigger), so no extra `docker compose up` task is strictly required in the vpn role.

No monitoring, metrics, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki, or log-shipping code exists in the repo today — this is a greenfield addition.</result>

# docker-otel-lgtm Components and Configuration

## Bundled Components

The image includes:
- **Grafana** (visualization)
- **Prometheus** (metrics)
- **Tempo** (traces)
- **Loki** (logs)
- **Pyroscope** (profiles)
- **OpenTelemetry Collector**
- **OBI** (optional eBPF auto-instrumentation)

Yes, Pyroscope for profiling is included.

## Production vs. Development Use

The README explicitly cautions: "If you are looking for a production-ready, out-of-the box solution to monitor applications and minimize MTTR...you should try Grafana Cloud Application Observability." The image is "intended for development, demo, and testing environments."

## Data Persistence & Retention

Components write to `/data` directory. You can mount external volumes for persistence. Retention is configurable via environment variables like `PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS="--storage.tsdb.retention.time=90d"` or `LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS="--limits.retention-period=90d"`. Custom config files can be mounted for deeper customization.

## Exposed Ports

Default OTLP endpoints: port 4317 (gRPC) and 4318 (HTTP). Grafana UI runs on port 3000.

## Configuration Methods

- Environment variables (`ENABLE_OBI`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`)
- `.env` file
- Mount custom configuration files
- `*_EXTRA_ARGS` variables for backend-specific CLI flags
- Grafana `GF_*` environment variables

## Overview

There are exporters that collect Xray (and V2Ray) metrics over its Stats API and export them to Prometheus. Several popular implementations are available on GitHub:

### Key Features

Traffic statistics include per-user, per-inbound, per-outbound data transfer metrics, as well as user activity metrics showing real-time user counts and connection patterns.

Enhanced user activity metrics are provided by parsing access logs.

### Configuration Requirements

The API and statistics-related features need to be enabled in your Xray (or V2Ray) config file. This requires setting up:

- A stats object, an api object with "StatsService" configured, policy settings with statsUserUplink and statsUserDownlink enabled, and proper routing rules

### StatsService API

The StatsService API can be queried using commands like StatsService.GetStats and StatsService.QueryStats to retrieve metrics including per-user traffic data like "user>>>u3@ws>>>traffic>>>uplink"

### Popular Implementations

Several GitHub projects provide Prometheus exporters for this purpose:
- wi1dcard/v2ray-exporter
- compassvpn/xray-exporter
- anatolykopyl/xray-exporter
- Computer-Cloud/xray-exporter

These exporters listen on port 9550 by default and can be configured with Prometheus using a scrape configuration.

**How should the central observability host be packaged? (It aggregates data from all VPN servers and holds the dashboards + retention.)**

Options:
- **All-in-one otel-lgtm** - Single grafana/otel-lgtm container (the one you referenced). Retention via PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS / LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS + a mounted /data volume. Bundles Grafana+Prometheus+Loki+Tempo+Pyroscope+OTel Collector. Grafana scopes it to dev/demo, but it's fine at single-operator scale and by far the least to operate.
- **Separate containers** - Grafana + Loki + Prometheus + Pyroscope as distinct compose services, each with its own config file for full control over retention/compaction. Production-grade but more moving parts to template and maintain.

**How deep should server-side instrumentation go? (Today the V2Ray config has no stats/api/policy — this directly answers your 'is there anything tunable on the server' question.)**

Options:
- **Full: traffic + host + logs** - Add api/stats/policy/routing to V2Ray config + a v2ray-exporter sidecar → per-user & per-inbound uplink/downlink bytes. Plus node_exporter + cAdvisor (host CPU/mem/disk/net, container stats) + nginx stub_status, and ship nginx/v2ray logs. The richest 'who used how much bandwidth' view.
- **Host + nginx + logs** - node_exporter + cAdvisor + nginx stub_status + log shipping, but leave the V2Ray VMess config completely untouched (no per-user traffic metrics). Lowest-risk to the proxy itself.
- **Logs only** - Just ship nginx/v2ray access+error logs to Loki. No exporters, no metrics, minimal footprint on each server.

**How should the per-server agents reach the central host, and how is the central Grafana exposed? (VPN servers are firewalled to 22/80/443 inbound only.)**

Options:
- **Reuse nginx + certbot TLS** - Central host runs the same nginx + Let's Encrypt pattern this repo already has. Agents push OUTBOUND to https://obs.<domain> with basic-auth/token; Grafana sits behind the same TLS+auth. No new inbound ports on any VPN server. Best reuse of existing repo conventions.
- **Private overlay (Tailscale/WG)** - Agents and Grafana are only reachable over a private mesh (Tailscale or WireGuard); nothing observability-related is public. Most secure, but adds a mesh dependency to install/manage on every host.
- **SSH reverse tunnel** - Agents ship metrics/logs through an SSH tunnel to the central host. No new public surface, reuses existing SSH access, but more fragile and fiddly to keep alive.

**Include profiling/traces now, or defer? (You mentioned Grafana Profiling specifically.)**

Options:
- **Defer / keep unused** - A VMess proxy emits no distributed traces and is not CPU-bound in a way worth profiling — metrics + logs deliver ~all the value. Pyroscope/Tempo stay present in the stack (they're bundled) but we don't wire agents to them yet. Dashboards focus on traffic/bandwidth/host health.
- **Include eBPF profiling** - Add a Grafana Alloy/OBI eBPF profiling agent (privileged) on each VPN server for continuous CPU profiles pushed to Pyroscope. Higher overhead and privilege on the proxy box for fairly marginal insight, but gives you the plug-and-play profiling dashboards you described.

# Plan: Centralized observability (Grafana LGTM) for a fleet of V2Ray servers

## Context

Today the repo runs a single-operator V2Ray VPN with **zero observability**: nginx and
v2ray write `access.log`/`error.log` to host bind mounts (`/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}`),
rotated by a `logrotate` cron; container stdout uses Docker's default `json-file` driver.
There is no metrics surface anywhere — the V2Ray config has **no `stats`/`api`/`policy`/`routing`**,
nginx has no `stub_status`, and there are no exporters, Prometheus, Grafana, or log shipping.

The goal is to scale this to **many VPN servers** with one central Grafana that:
1. collects logs **and** metrics from every server,
2. enforces **retention** so storage doesn't blow up,
3. serves **pre-built, plug-and-play dashboards** with a top-of-dashboard **`$server` dropdown**
   that auto-lists whatever servers are currently reporting (new server plugs in → appears in the
   dropdown, no dashboard edits),
4. answers the open question *"is there anything worth tuning server-side?"* — **yes**: enabling the
   V2Ray StatsService gives per-user / per-inbound uplink-downlink byte counters, which is the single
   most valuable server-side knob (most other V2Ray tuning genuinely is client-side).

### Assumed decisions (I chose the recommended option on each; flip any if wrong)
- **Central stack packaging:** all-in-one `grafana/otel-lgtm` (the image you referenced). Retention is
  configurable via `PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS` / `LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS` + a mounted `/data` volume, and it
  bundles Grafana + Prometheus + Loki + Tempo + Pyroscope + OTel Collector. Grafana scopes it to
  "dev/demo," but it's the right pragmatic choice at single-operator / handful-of-servers scale.
- **Server-side depth:** **Full** — V2Ray traffic stats + host metrics + nginx + log shipping.
- **Ingest / exposure:** **reuse this repo's nginx + certbot Let's Encrypt pattern** on the central
  host. Agents push **outbound** over HTTPS; no new inbound ports on any VPN server.
- **Profiling / traces:** **deferred**. A VMess proxy emits no distributed traces and isn't worth
  CPU-profiling; metrics + logs carry ~all the value. Pyroscope/Tempo stay present (bundled) but
  unwired. Dashboards focus on traffic / bandwidth / host health / logs.

---

## Architecture

Two additions, each following an existing pattern in the repo.

\```
 VPN server (existing /opt/vpn compose project)          Central host (NEW /opt/obs project)
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ v2ray ─(StatsService gRPC :api_port)─┐     │          │ nginx + certbot  (reused pattern)     │
 │ nginx ─(stub_status, localhost)──┐   │     │  HTTPS   │   /       → grafana:3000 (Grafana auth)│
 │ node_exporter, cadvisor ─────┐   │   │     │  OTLP    │   /otlp   → otel-lgtm:4318 (basic-auth)│
 │ log files (bind mount) ──┐   │   │   │     │  push    │                                        │
 │                          ▼   ▼   ▼   ▼     │ ───────► │ otel-lgtm: Prometheus+Loki+Grafana     │
 │              Grafana Alloy (single agent)  │ outbound │   retention via *_EXTRA_ARGS           │
 │              scrape + tail → OTLP export ──┼──────────┤   /data on a persistent host volume    │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────┘   443    └──────────────────────────────────────┘
     firewall: 22/80/443 in only; agent egresses on 443       new inventory group [observability]
\```

**Why Grafana Alloy as the single per-server agent:** it does Prometheus scraping, log-file tailing,
relabeling (to stamp the per-server label), and OTLP export in one process — a cleaner fit for the
LGTM backend than stitching promtail + a prometheus agent + the OTel collector. Everything ships as
**OTLP/HTTP to one endpoint** (`/otlp`), so the central host needs exactly one authenticated ingest
route behind the existing nginx+TLS.

**Why outbound-only / OTLP:** VPN servers stay firewalled to 22/80/443 inbound (per
`firewall_allowed_tcp` in `group_vars/all.yml`). All exporters stay on the internal compose bridge
(`expose:`, never `ports:`), and Alloy egresses on 443 — so **no firewall changes on VPN servers**
and no metrics surface exposed to the internet.

**Plug-and-play `$server` dropdown:** Alloy stamps every metric/log with a `server` label
(= `monitoring_server_label`, defaulting to `inventory_hostname`). Provisioned dashboards define
`$server = label_values(server)`. A newly-deployed server shows up in the dropdown automatically —
no dashboard edits.

## Part A — Per-server agent + exporters (extends the existing `vpn` role)

All changes keep the tracked `server/…` truth-source and the rendered `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/…`
`.j2` in lockstep (repo rule). Everything is gated behind a `monitoring_enabled` flag so it can be
switched off per host/group.

1. **V2Ray config — enable StatsService** (`ansible/roles/vpn/templates/v2ray/config.json.j2`
   + `server/templates/v2ray/config.json.tmpl`). Add, alongside the existing vmess inbound/freedom
   outbound:
   - `"stats": {}`
   - `"api": { "tag": "api", "services": ["StatsService"] }`
   - `"policy": { "levels": {"1": {"statsUserUplink": true, "statsUserDownlink": true}},
     "system": {"statsInboundUplink": true, "statsInboundDownlink": true,
     "statsOutboundUplink": true, "statsOutboundDownlink": true} }`
   - a `"tag": "proxy"` on the existing vmess inbound, and an `"email"` on the client (so a
     `user>>>…>>>traffic` stat key exists for per-user breakdown)
   - a second inbound: `dokodemo-door` on `127.0.0.1`-of-the-compose-network, port
     `{{ v2ray_api_port }}`, `"tag": "api"` (exposed internally only — reached by the exporter over
     the compose network, never host-published)
   - `"routing": { "rules": [{"type": "field", "inboundTag": ["api"], "outboundTag": "api"}] }`

2. **nginx `stub_status`** (`ansible/roles/vpn/templates/nginx/v2ray.conf.j2` + `.tmpl`): add an
   internal-only `server { listen 127.0.0.1:<port>; location /nginx_status { stub_status; } }` (or a
   `location` restricted to the compose network) for the nginx exporter to scrape. Does **not** touch
   the public 80/443 server blocks.

3. **New compose services** appended to `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/compose.yml.j2` +
   `server/compose.yml`, each `expose:`-only (no `ports:`), all `{% if monitoring_enabled %}`-guarded:
   - `v2ray-exporter` — `wi1dcard/v2ray-exporter`, points at `v2ray:{{ v2ray_api_port }}` → per-user/
     per-inbound uplink/downlink byte metrics.
   - `node-exporter` — `prom/node-exporter`, host `/proc`,`/sys`,`/` mounted read-only.
   - `cadvisor` — `gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor`, per-container CPU/mem/net.
   - `nginx-exporter` — `nginx/nginx-prometheus-exporter`, scrapes the stub_status listener.
   - `alloy` — `grafana/alloy`, mounts `runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}` read-only + its rendered config;
     scrapes the four exporters, tails the log files, and OTLP-pushes to `{{ obs_endpoint }}` with
     basic-auth.

4. **Alloy config template** — new `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/alloy/config.alloy.j2`
   + `server/templates/alloy/config.alloy.tmpl`. `prometheus.scrape` the exporters,
   `loki.source.file` the log files, relabel to add `server="{{ monitoring_server_label }}"`, export
   via `otelcol.exporter.otlphttp` to `{{ obs_endpoint }}`. Render task + `runtime/alloy` dir added to
   `ansible/roles/vpn/tasks/main.yml` (mirror the existing `runtime/v2ray` dir-create + render +

5. **New variables**:
   - `ansible/group_vars/all.yml`: `monitoring_enabled: false` (opt-in), `v2ray_api_port: 10085`,

   - Secrets via the established `vault_* → plain-name` indirection
     (`ansible/group_vars/vpn/vars.yml` + `vault.yml`): `obs_ingest_user`, `obs_ingest_password`.
   - No `firewall_allowed_tcp` change (egress-only).

## Part B — Central observability host (NEW, mirrors vpn + letsencrypt patterns)

1. **Inventory**: add `[observability]` group + `[observability:vars]` to
   `ansible/inventory/prod.ini.example` (and the real gitignored `prod.ini`). One host to start.

2. **group_vars**: `ansible/group_vars/observability/vars.yml` +
   `vault.yml.example` — `obs_domain`, `obs_letsencrypt_email`, `grafana_admin_password`, and the
   `obs_ingest_user`/`obs_ingest_password` that must match Part A. Retention knobs:
   `loki_retention: 30d` (logs are the space hog), `prometheus_retention: 90d` (metrics are cheap).

3. **New role `ansible/roles/observability/`** — self-contained (does **not** couple to the `vpn`
   role's templates), rendering a compose project into a separate `deploy_path` (`/opt/obs`):
   - `otel-lgtm` service — pinned image tag, `PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS=--storage.tsdb.retention.time={{ prometheus_retention }}`,
     `LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS=--limits.retention-period={{ loki_retention }}`, `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD`,
     and a **named/host volume mounted at `/data`** for persistence across redeploys.
   - `nginx` + `certbot` — copied from the vpn role's proven templates, retargeted: TLS-terminate
     `obs_domain`, reverse-proxy `/` → `otel-lgtm:3000` and `/otlp` → `otel-lgtm:4318` with
     `auth_basic` for ingest. Reuse the **two-phase Let's Encrypt bootstrap** logic from
     `ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml` (acme-only conf → certbot --webroot → full conf →
     compose up), inlined into this role so it stays decoupled.
   - **Grafana provisioning**: mount datasource + dashboard-provider YAML and dashboard JSON into the
     otel-lgtm Grafana provisioning dir. Tracked assets live under `server/observability/` (compose
     tmpl, nginx tmpl, grafana provisioning, `dashboards/*.json`).

4. **Dashboards** (`server/observability/dashboards/*.json`, provisioned): each defines
   `$server = label_values(server)` at the top. Panels — bandwidth in/out per server (v2ray inbound
   stats + node_exporter net), per-user traffic (v2ray user stats), active connections
   (nginx stub_status), host CPU/mem/disk, container health (cadvisor), and a Loki logs panel filtered
   by `$server`. Start with one "Fleet overview" + one "Per-server drilldown" dashboard.

5. **Playbook + Justfile + docs**: `ansible/playbooks/observability.yml` (targets `[observability]`,
   runs `common` + `docker` + `observability`); Justfile recipes `deploy-obs`, `logs-obs`,
   `ps-obs`; `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` covering the architecture, retention sizing, and adding a server.

## Retention / storage sizing (the "will blow up" concern)

- **Logs (Loki)** are the space hog on a VPN. Cap with `--limits.retention-period` (e.g. 30d) + the
  compactor; consider raising V2Ray `loglevel` from `warning` only if you want access-log-derived
  metrics (more volume). Keep access logs at `warning`/off unless needed.
- **Metrics (Prometheus)** for a handful of hosts at 15–60s scrape are tiny; `--storage.tsdb.retention.time=90d`
  is comfortable on a modest disk. Optionally add `--storage.tsdb.retention.size`.
- **Persistence**: mount `/data` to a host volume so retention survives `docker compose` recreation.
- Document expected disk (rule of thumb: metrics ≪ 1 GB/host/90d; logs dominate and scale with traffic).

**Create (per-server):** `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/alloy/config.alloy.j2` + `server/templates/alloy/config.alloy.tmpl`.

**Create (central host):**
- `ansible/roles/observability/` (tasks/templates/defaults/handlers).

- `ansible/playbooks/observability.yml`.

- `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`; `[observability]` group in `ansible/inventory/prod.ini.example`.
- `Justfile` recipes: `deploy-obs`, `logs-obs`, `ps-obs`.

**Reuse (don't reinvent):** the two-phase cert bootstrap in `ansible/roles/letsencrypt/tasks/main.yml`,
the nginx TLS/WS templates `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/nginx/{v2ray,acme-only}.conf.j2`, the

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Plan: Centralized observability (Grafana LGTM) for a fleet of V2Ray servers

## Context

Today the repo runs a single-operator V2Ray VPN with **zero observability**: nginx and
v2ray write `access.log`/`error.log` to host bind mounts (`/opt/vpn/runtime/logs/{nginx,v2ray}`),
rotated by a `logrotate` cron; container stdout uses Docker's default `json-file` driver.
There is no metrics surface anywhere — the V2Ray config has **no `stats`/`api`/`policy`/`routing`**,
nginx has no `stub_status`, and there are no exporters, Prometheus, Grafana, or log shipping.

The goal is to scale this to **many VPN servers** with one central Grafana that:
1. collects logs **and** metrics from every server,
2. enforces **retention** so storage doesn't blow up,
3. serves **pre-built, plug-and-play dashboards** with a top-of-dashboard **`$server` dropdown**
   that auto-lists whatever servers are currently reporting (new server plugs in → appears in the
   dropdown, no dashboard edits),
4. answers the open question *"is there anything worth tuning server-side?"* — **yes**: enabling the
   V2Ray StatsService gives per-user / per-inbound uplink-downlink byte counters, which is the single
   most valuable server-side knob (most other V2Ray tuning genuinely is client-side).

### Assumed decisions (I chose the recommended option on each; flip any if wrong)
- **Central stack packaging:** all-in-one `grafana/otel-lgtm` (the image you referenced). Retention is
  configurable via `PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS` / `LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS` + a mounted `/data` volume, and it
  bundles Grafana + Prometheus + Loki + Tempo + Pyroscope + OTel Collector. Grafana scopes it to
  "dev/demo," but it's the right pragmatic choice at single-operator / handful-of-servers scale.
- **Server-side depth:** **Full** — V2Ray traffic stats + host metrics + nginx + log shipping.
- **Ingest / exposure:** **reuse this repo's nginx + certbot Let's Encrypt pattern** on the central
  host. Agents push **outbound** over HTTPS; no new inbound ports on any VPN server.
- **Profiling / traces:** **deferred**. A VMess proxy emits no distributed traces and isn't worth
  CPU-profiling; metrics + logs carry ~all the value. Pyroscope/Tempo stay present (bundled) but
  unwired. Dashboards focus on traffic / bandwidth / host health / logs.

---

## Architecture

Two additions, each following an existing pattern in the repo.

```
 VPN server (existing /opt/vpn compose project)          Central host (NEW /opt/obs project)
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ v2ray ─(StatsService gRPC :api_port)─┐     │          │ nginx + certbot  (reused pattern)     │
 │ nginx ─(stub_status, localhost)──┐   │     │  HTTPS   │   /       → grafana:3000 (Grafana auth)│
 │ node_exporter, cadvisor ─────┐   │   │     │  OTLP    │   /otlp   → otel-lgtm:4318 (basic-auth)│
 │ log files (bind mount) ──┐   │   │   │     │  push    │                                        │
 │                          ▼   ▼   ▼   ▼     │ ───────► │ otel-lgtm: Prometheus+Loki+Grafana     │
 │              Grafana Alloy (single agent)  │ outbound │   retention via *_EXTRA_ARGS           │
 │              scrape + tail → OTLP export ──┼──────────┤   /data on a persistent host volume    │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────┘   443    └──────────────────────────────────────┘
     firewall: 22/80/443 in only; agent egresses on 443       new inventory group [observability]
```

**Why Grafana Alloy as the single per-server agent:** it does Prometheus scraping, log-file tailing,
relabeling (to stamp the per-server label), and OTLP export in one process — a cleaner fit for the
LGTM backend than stitching promtail + a prometheus agent + the OTel collector. Everything ships as
**OTLP/HTTP to one endpoint** (`/otlp`), so the central host needs exactly one authenticated ingest
route behind the existing nginx+TLS.

**Why outbound-only / OTLP:** VPN servers stay firewalled to 22/80/443 inbound (per
`firewall_allowed_tcp` in `group_vars/all.yml`). All exporters stay on the internal compose bridge
(`expose:`, never `ports:`), and Alloy egresses on 443 — so **no firewall changes on VPN servers**
and no metrics surface exposed to the internet.

**Plug-and-play `$server` dropdown:** Alloy stamps every metric/log with a `server` label
(= `monitoring_server_label`, defaulting to `inventory_hostname`). Provisioned dashboards define
`$server = label_values(server)`. A newly-deployed server shows up in the dropdown automatically —
no dashboard edits.

19	    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/{{ domain }}/privkey.pem;
20	    include /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-nginx.conf;
21	    ssl_dhparam /etc/letsencrypt/ssl-dhparams.pem;
22	
23	
24	    root /usr/share/nginx/html/v2ray;
25	    index index.html;
26	
27	    location {{ v2ray_ws_path }} {
28	        proxy_redirect off;
29	        proxy_pass http://v2ray:{{ v2ray_internal_port }};
30	        proxy_http_version 1.1;
31	        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
32	        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
33	        proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
34	
35	        # Keep long-lived / idle WebSocket tunnels alive. nginx's default
36	        # proxy_read_timeout is 60s, which severs any tunnel with no upstream
37	        # data for 60s — e.g. an LLM streaming response that pauses while the
38	        # model "thinks", or an idle SSH-over-proxy session → the client sees
39	        # "other side closed" at ~60s. Raise well above interactive gaps.
40	        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
41	        proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
42	    }
43	}
44

1	# Laptop-side wrapper for ansible deploys.

10	ansible_opts := env_var_or_default("ANSIBLE_OPTS", "")

15	# One-time laptop setup: install ansible, jq, uv (brew/apt auto-detected) and fetch ansible-galaxy collections. Idempotent.
16	setup:
17	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
18	    set -euo pipefail
19	
20	    missing=()
21	    for t in ansible jq uv; do
22	        command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$t")
23	    done
24	
25	    if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
26	        echo "[setup] ansible, jq, uv already on PATH — nothing to install."
27	    else
28	        echo "[setup] Missing: ${missing[*]}"
29	        if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
30	            echo "[setup] Using Homebrew."
31	            brew install "${missing[@]}"
32	        elif [ -f /etc/os-release ] && grep -qiE '^ID(_LIKE)?=.*(debian|ubuntu)' /etc/os-release; then
33	            echo "[setup] Using apt (Debian/Ubuntu detected)."
34	            apt_pkgs=()
35	            install_uv=0
36	            for t in "${missing[@]}"; do
37	                case "$t" in
38	                    ansible|jq) apt_pkgs+=("$t") ;;
39	                    uv)         install_uv=1 ;;
40	                esac
41	            done
42	            if [ ${#apt_pkgs[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
43	                sudo apt-get update
44	                sudo apt-get install -y "${apt_pkgs[@]}"
45	            fi
46	            # uv isn't in Debian/Ubuntu apt yet; use Astral's official installer
47	            # (lands in ~/.local/bin — make sure that's on PATH afterwards).
48	            if [ $install_uv -eq 1 ]; then
49	                echo "[setup] Installing uv via astral.sh installer..."
50	                curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
51	            fi
52	        else
53	            echo "[setup] No brew or apt detected on this OS." >&2
54	            echo "[setup] Install manually: ${missing[*]}" >&2
55	            echo "[setup] See README.md 'Deploy' section for install options." >&2
56	            exit 1
57	        fi
58	    fi
59	
60	    echo "[setup] Fetching ansible-galaxy collections..."
61	    cd {{ansible_dir}} && ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml
62	
63	    if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then

66	        echo "          brew install azure-cli     # macOS / Linuxbrew"

173	az-up *args:

189	az-rotate-ip *args:

192	# List every tracked Azure VM (.secrets/azure/vms/*.json). '*' marks the vms/current target.
193	az-list:
194	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
195	    set -euo pipefail
196	    VMS_DIR=".secrets/azure/vms"
197	    if [ ! -d "$VMS_DIR" ] || ! compgen -G "$VMS_DIR/*.json" >/dev/null; then
198	        echo "No tracked VMs. Run 'just az-up' to provision one."
199	        exit 0
200	    fi
201	    command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo "[az-list] jq not on PATH (brew install jq)" >&2; exit 1; }
202	    current=""
203	    if [ -L "$VMS_DIR/current" ]; then
204	        current=$(basename "$(readlink "$VMS_DIR/current")" .json)
205	    fi
206	    printf '%s %-32s %-55s %-18s %s\n' ' ' 'RG' 'FQDN' 'PUBLIC_IP' 'CREATED_AT'
207	    printf '%s %-32s %-55s %-18s %s\n' ' ' '--' '----' '---------' '----------'
208	    for f in "$VMS_DIR"/*.json; do
209	        base=$(basename "$f")
210	        [ "$base" = "current" ] && continue
211	        rg=$(jq -r '.rg // "?"' "$f")
212	        fqdn=$(jq -r '.fqdn // "?"' "$f")
213	        ip=$(jq -r '.public_ip // "?"' "$f")
214	        created=$(jq -r '.created_at // "?"' "$f")
215	        marker=' '
216	        [ "$rg" = "$current" ] && marker='*'
217	        printf '%s %-32s %-55s %-18s %s\n' "$marker" "$rg" "$fqdn" "$ip" "$created"
218	    done

221	az-cycle:
222	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
223	    set -euo pipefail
224	    scripts/az_up.sh

226	    echo "[az-cycle] Tracking RG=$RG for this cycle."

233	    echo

# V2Ray Exporter Command-Line Usage

**Endpoint Flag:**
`--v2ray-endpoint "127.0.0.1:54321"` points to the V2Ray API endpoint.

**Listen Port & Path:**
The exporter listens on `:9550` by default. The metrics are exposed at `/scrape` path:
> "metrics_path: /scrape"

**Docker Image:**
> "docker run --rm -d wi1dcard/v2ray-exporter:master"

Note: `latest` tag is unavailable; use `master` for the latest build.

**V2Ray Configuration Requirements:**
Yes, the V2Ray config must enable:
- `stats` section
- `api` section with `StatsService`
- `policy` settings with user/system statistics enabled
- An API inbound listening on a specific port (e.g., 54321)

**Key Metric Names Exposed:**
- `v2ray_up` (scrape success indicator)
- `v2ray_uptime_seconds`
- `v2ray_goroutines`
- `v2ray_memstats_alloc_bytes`
- `v2ray_traffic_uplink_bytes_total{dimension="inbound|outbound|user",target="name"}`
- `v2ray_traffic_downlink_bytes_total{dimension="inbound|outbound|user",target="name"}`
```

```j2
// Grafana Alloy — per-VPN-server metrics + log shipper.
// Rendered by the vpn role (only when monitoring_enabled). Scrapes the local
// exporters over the compose network, tails the nginx/v2ray log files, stamps a
// `server` label on everything (drives the Grafana $server dropdown), and pushes
// OUTBOUND over HTTPS with basic auth to the central observability host. No
// inbound ports are involved.

// ---------- Metrics: scrape local exporters, remote_write to the central Prometheus ----------
prometheus.scrape "exporters" {
  targets = [
    {"__address__" = "v2ray-exporter:9550", "__metrics_path__" = "/scrape", "job" = "v2ray",    "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
    {"__address__" = "node-exporter:9100",                                   "job" = "node",     "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
    {"__address__" = "cadvisor:8080",                                        "job" = "cadvisor", "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
    {"__address__" = "nginx-exporter:9113",                                  "job" = "nginx",    "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
  ]
  scrape_interval = "30s"
  forward_to      = [prometheus.remote_write.obs.receiver]
}

prometheus.remote_write "obs" {
  endpoint {
    url = "{{ obs_base_url }}/prom/api/v1/write"
    basic_auth {
      username = "{{ obs_ingest_user }}"
      password = "{{ obs_ingest_password }}"
    }
  }
}

// ---------- Logs: tail nginx + v2ray files, push to the central Loki ----------
local.file_match "vpn_logs" {
  path_targets = [
    {"__path__" = "/var/log/nginx/*.log", "job" = "nginx", "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
    {"__path__" = "/var/log/v2ray/*.log", "job" = "v2ray", "server" = "{{ monitoring_server_label }}"},
  ]
}

loki.source.file "vpn_logs" {
  targets    = local.file_match.vpn_logs.targets
  forward_to = [loki.write.obs.receiver]
}

loki.write "obs" {
  endpoint {
    url = "{{ obs_base_url }}/loki/loki/api/v1/push"
    basic_auth {
      username = "{{ obs_ingest_user }}"
      password = "{{ obs_ingest_password }}"
    }
  }
}

```

```text
# Custom Dashboards and Configuration for docker-otel-lgtm

## Adding Custom Grafana Dashboards

The documentation specifies the exact provisioning path:

**Dashboard Provider YAML Location:**
Mount your provisioning configuration to: `"/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom.yaml:ro"`

**Dashboard JSON Location:**
Mount dashboard files to: `"/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom/custom-dashboard.json:ro"`

Example docker-compose configuration:
```
volumes:
  - ./custom-dashboard.json:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom/custom-dashboard.json:ro
  - ./dashboards-provisioning.yaml:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom.yaml:ro
```

To set a custom home dashboard, use: `GF_DASHBOARDS_DEFAULT_HOME_DASHBOARD_PATH=/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom/custom-dashboard.json`

## Data Persistence

Components write to the `/data` directory inside the container. Mount a volume there to persist data: `docker run -v ./my-volume:/data grafana/otel-lgtm`

## Backend Arguments and Extra Configuration

Use these environment variables to pass CLI flags without modifying files:
- `PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS` — e.g., `"--storage.tsdb.retention.time=90d"`
- `LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS` — e.g., `"--limits.retention-period=90d"`

Example: `docker run -e PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS="--storage.tsdb.retention.time=90d" grafana/otel-lgtm`

## Internal Ports

The documentation does not explicitly list the internal container ports where Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, and Tempo listen.

---
# otel-lgtm all-in-one: Grafana + Prometheus + Loki + Tempo + Pyroscope + OTel
# Collector. Uses :latest to match the repo's other images (nginx, certbot,
# v2ray); pin a specific tag here for reproducibility if you prefer.
obs_lgtm_image: "grafana/otel-lgtm:latest"

# Retention (see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md "Retention & sizing"). Logs are the space
# hog → shorter; metrics are cheap → longer.
prometheus_retention: "90d"
loki_retention: "30d"

# Internal container ports of the otel-lgtm backends (nginx reverse-proxies these).
obs_grafana_port: 3000
obs_prometheus_port: 9090
obs_loki_port: 3100

# Grafana provisioning assets (dashboards + provider yaml) synced to the host.
obs_grafana_src: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../../server/observability/grafana"

# Let's Encrypt knobs (self-contained here — this role doesn't use the vpn's
# letsencrypt role). Set le_staging: 1 to hit the staging CA while testing.
le_rsa_key_size: 4096
le_staging: 0

```

```j2
# Central observability front. TLS-terminates {{ obs_domain }} and:
#   /prom/*  → Prometheus remote-write receiver (agents push metrics)  [basic-auth]
#   /loki/*  → Loki push API (agents push logs)                        [basic-auth]
#   /*       → Grafana UI (its own login)
# All three backends run inside the single otel-lgtm container.

# WebSocket upgrade map for Grafana Live (valid in the http{} context that
# conf.d files are included into).
map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
    default upgrade;
    ''      close;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name {{ obs_domain }};

    location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ {
        root /var/www/certbot;
    }

    location / {
        return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
    }
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name {{ obs_domain }};

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/{{ obs_domain }}/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/{{ obs_domain }}/privkey.pem;
    include /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-nginx.conf;
    ssl_dhparam /etc/letsencrypt/ssl-dhparams.pem;

    # Agents remote-write metrics here. Trailing slash on proxy_pass strips the
    # /prom prefix → Prometheus receives /api/v1/write.
    location /prom/ {
        auth_basic "obs-ingest";
        auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/ingest.htpasswd;
        proxy_pass http://otel-lgtm:{{ obs_prometheus_port }}/;
        client_max_body_size 32m;
    }

    # Agents push logs here. No trailing slash on proxy_pass → the /loki/... path
    # is preserved, and Loki's native push path is /loki/api/v1/push.
    location /loki/ {
        auth_basic "obs-ingest";
        auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/ingest.htpasswd;
        proxy_pass http://otel-lgtm:{{ obs_loki_port }};
        client_max_body_size 32m;
    }

    # Grafana UI (has its own auth). Root last so the ingest prefixes win.
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://otel-lgtm:{{ obs_grafana_port }};
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
    }
}

```

# Rendered by ansible/roles/observability — edits here are overwritten on next deploy.
services:
  otel-lgtm:
    image: {{ obs_lgtm_image }}
    container_name: otel-lgtm
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD={{ grafana_admin_password }}
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://{{ obs_domain }}
      # Retention + enable the Prometheus remote-write receiver so agents can push.
      - PROMETHEUS_EXTRA_ARGS=--storage.tsdb.retention.time={{ prometheus_retention }} --web.enable-remote-write-receiver
      - LOKI_EXTRA_ARGS=--limits.retention-period={{ loki_retention }}
    volumes:
      # Persist all backend data (TSDB, Loki chunks, etc.) across recreations.
      - obs-data:/data
      # Provisioned dashboards (plug-and-play, $server-templated).
      - ./runtime/grafana/dashboards.yaml:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom.yaml:ro
      - ./runtime/grafana/dashboards:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards/custom:ro
    expose:
      - "{{ obs_grafana_port }}"
      - "{{ obs_prometheus_port }}"
      - "{{ obs_loki_port }}"

  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    container_name: obs-nginx
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./runtime/nginx/conf.d:/etc/nginx/conf.d:ro
      - ./runtime/nginx/ingest.htpasswd:/etc/nginx/ingest.htpasswd:ro
      - ./runtime/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt
      - ./runtime/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    depends_on:
      - otel-lgtm
    command: "/bin/sh -c 'while :; do sleep 6h & wait $${!}; nginx -s reload; done & nginx -g \"daemon off;\"'"

  certbot:
    image: certbot/certbot
    container_name: obs-certbot
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./runtime/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt
      - ./runtime/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot
    entrypoint: "/bin/sh -c 'trap exit TERM; while :; do certbot renew; sleep 12h & wait $${!}; done;'"

volumes:
  obs-data:

```yaml
---
# Central observability host: renders the otel-lgtm + nginx + certbot stack into
# {{ deploy_path }} (/opt/obs) and brings it up, using the same two-phase Let's
# Encrypt bootstrap the VPN stack uses. Self-contained — does NOT depend on the
# vpn or letsencrypt roles' templates. See docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.

- name: Create obs deploy directory tree
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ item }}"
    state: directory
    owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    mode: "0755"
  loop:
    - "{{ deploy_path }}"
    - "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime"
    - "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/conf.d"
    - "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/grafana"
    - "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf"
    - "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/www"

- name: Sync Grafana provisioning assets (dashboards + provider)
  ansible.posix.synchronize:
    src: "{{ obs_grafana_src }}/"
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/grafana/"
    delete: true
    recursive: true
    private_key: "{{ ansible_private_key_file | default(ansible_ssh_private_key_file) | default(omit) }}"
  delegate_to: localhost
  become: false

- name: Render obs compose.yml
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: compose.yml.j2
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/compose.yml"
    owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    mode: "0644"
  notify: recreate obs stack

- name: Render ingest htpasswd
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: nginx/ingest.htpasswd.j2
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/ingest.htpasswd"
    owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    mode: "0640"
  notify: reload obs nginx

- name: Ensure certbot TLS options file is present
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/certbot/certbot/master/certbot-nginx/certbot_nginx/_internal/tls_configs/options-ssl-nginx.conf
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/options-ssl-nginx.conf"
    mode: "0644"
    force: false

- name: Ensure DH parameters file is present
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/certbot/certbot/master/certbot/certbot/ssl-dhparams.pem
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/ssl-dhparams.pem"
    mode: "0644"
    force: false

- name: Check if obs cert already exists
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/certbot/conf/live/{{ obs_domain }}/fullchain.pem"
  register: obs_cert

- name: Render full obs nginx config (cert present)
  when: obs_cert.stat.exists
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: nginx/obs.conf.j2
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/conf.d/obs.conf"
    owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    mode: "0644"
  notify: reload obs nginx

- name: Render ACME-only obs nginx config (first-run bootstrap)
  when: not obs_cert.stat.exists
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: nginx/acme-only.conf.j2
    dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/conf.d/obs.conf"
    owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    mode: "0644"

- name: Bootstrap Let's Encrypt certificate (obs)
  when: not obs_cert.stat.exists
  block:
    - name: Start obs nginx with ACME-only config
      community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
        project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
        services:
          - nginx
        state: present

    - name: Wait for obs nginx to respond on ACME path
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "http://{{ obs_domain }}/.well-known/acme-challenge/healthcheck"
        status_code: [200, 404]
      register: obs_acme_probe
      retries: 15
      delay: 3
      until: obs_acme_probe.status in [200, 404]

    - name: Request real certificate from Let's Encrypt (obs)
      # One line to avoid YAML folded-scalar indentation quirks (see the vpn
      # letsencrypt role for the same rationale).
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv:
          - docker
          - compose
          - run
          - --rm
          - --entrypoint
          - >-
            certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/certbot
            {% if le_staging | int == 1 %}--staging {% endif %}
            --email {{ letsencrypt_email }} -d {{ obs_domain }}
            --rsa-key-size {{ le_rsa_key_size }}
            --agree-tos --non-interactive --no-eff-email
          - certbot
        chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
      register: obs_certbot_result
      changed_when: "'Successfully received certificate' in obs_certbot_result.stdout or 'Certificate not yet due for renewal' in obs_certbot_result.stdout"

    - name: Render full obs nginx config now that cert exists
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: nginx/obs.conf.j2
        dest: "{{ deploy_path }}/runtime/nginx/conf.d/obs.conf"
        owner: "{{ ansible_user }}"
        group: "{{ ansible_user }}"
        mode: "0644"

- name: Bring up full obs stack
  community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    project_src: "{{ deploy_path }}"
    state: present

- name: Reload obs nginx after bootstrap
  ansible.builtin.shell: docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -s reload
  args:
    chdir: "{{ deploy_path }}"
  when: not obs_cert.stat.exists
  changed_when: true

```
